title: Choose Catch's art direction
question: Each card is a whole world for Catch, sketched on a phone. Keep the roll, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: The Handscroll
options.lineage: Japanese illustrated handscrolls, by way of Peach Momoko's ink and watercolor
options.thesis: Your archive as a hand-painted scroll that unrolls one scene per catch.
options.viewport: The scroll runs sideways across the screen, today's catch painted largest on the right with its seal; the paste slot rests below like a brush stand.
options.risk: Sideways scrolling is slower for scanning hundreds of links, so search and a plain list view must carry that load.

raised.raise: One dial drives the whole scroll: a catch's age sets its ink, wet and vivid when new, faded into the paper when old.
Strict size steps: the newest catch is painted at full height, older ones step down in three fixed sizes, never in between.
Vermilion has one job only: the seal on a session that's still open. Close it and the seal lifts.

options.label: The Concierge Desk
options.lineage: the front desk of a grand old hotel, framed like a paused film still
options.thesis: Every catch is a numbered room; its key hangs in a pigeonhole until you check out.
options.viewport: A symmetrical wall of pigeonholes with brass room numbers; open sessions hold a key, closed ones sit empty; a desk bell is the Catch button.
options.risk: Topped my own list, and film-still symmetry is where many runs land; it has to own its palette and never copy a director's type tricks.

options.label: Catalogue Sleeve
options.thesis: Each catch is a numbered release on a matte black sleeve; your saving rhythm draws the pulse plot.
options.viewport: Matte black field, a stacked white-line plot drawn from when you caught each link, the session number as the only headline.
options.case: Session numbers already are catalogue numbers and album-cover culture fits you; colder than the warmth your references share.
options.risk: Coded colour labels can hide what a link is, so titles must stay readable.

options.label: Screening Room
options.lineage: cinema one-sheets on a streaming title wall
options.thesis: Each catch becomes a film one-sheet; folders are rows in your private cinema.
options.viewport: Rows of poster tiles per folder; the poster you land on grows and shows its title card while the rest of the wall dims.
options.case: Speaks to your love of film and is very clear, but the wall pattern is the most familiar layout on your phone.
options.risk: Without real artwork per link, posters slide toward generic coloured tiles.

options.label: Departure Board
options.lineage: boarding passes and split-flap gate boards
options.thesis: Every catch is a boarding pass; the board lists sessions and flags what is still open.
options.viewport: Split-flap board of session numbers and titles up top; the newest pass tears off just above the paste slot.
options.case: Fuses cleanly (sessions as flight numbers, open and closed as boarding status) and reads clearly, but none of your references live here.
options.risk: Reads as a travel app before it reads as art.

options.label: Live Type Specimen
options.thesis: One giant letter that morphs as you drag a dial.
options.viewport: A single huge glyph over a breathing grid.
options.risk: Nothing to do with saving links.
options.case: Fuses poorly: type sliders have no job in a link archive.
options.kept: One dial drives the whole surface (a catch's age sets its ink everywhere).

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.viewport: A towering pixel headline over dense columns.
options.case: Fuses poorly: neither you nor the archive live in pixel type.
options.kept: Fixed size steps instead of anything in between.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Yellow sign bands pointing to each session.
options.viewport: Overhead yellow bands with monumental numbers.
options.risk: A sign system, not an artwork.
options.case: Fuses poorly: wayfinding solves a problem Catch doesn't have.
options.kept: One colour reserved for one job only.

canonCard.label: Clean read-later list
canonCard.thesis: What link-saving apps ship, done very well.
canonCard.viewport: A tidy list of titles with site icons and an add field.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other read-later app by design.
